claims.text: The nanoparticles are multi-element, near-equiatomic solid solutions with initially clean surfaces.
Formation of a stable surface oxide layer governs the high-temperature structural stability of the nanoparticles.
Formation of a stable surface oxide layer governs the high-temperature chemical stability of the nanoparticles.
The stable oxide layer acts as a barrier to further oxidation.
The stable oxide layer prevents degradation of the nanoparticles.
Nanoparticles bearing a stable oxide layer will oxidize more slowly than nanoparticles without such a layer.
Nanoparticles bearing a stable oxide layer will undergo less structural and chemical degradation than nanoparticles without such a layer.
Nanoparticles without a stable oxide layer will undergo rapid oxidation under the stated high-temperature regimes.
Nanoparticles without a stable oxide layer will undergo rapid degradation under the stated high-temperature regimes.
For protection to be effective, the stable oxide layer must form below the onset temperature of significant oxidation and degradation.
A controlled atmosphere is required to prevent continued oxidation of the nanoparticles.
